To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HDL is physically altered by inflammation, that this alteration affects the function of the HDL particle, and that this alteration is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular disease.
HDL is a key component of the innate immune system and is a key regulator of inflammatory cytokine signalling.
HDLc biophysical properties are modified by pro‐inflammatory cytokines and that this modification is related to the pro‐inflammatory state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that cytokine signalling plays in the regulation of HDLc and its ability to function in reverse cholesterol transport.
the effects of cytokines and inflammation on HDLc metabolism.
the role that HDLc plays as a modulator of the immune response, particularly in the context of inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of HDLc is not as clear as it was once believed.
the inflammatory state is an important factor in determining HDLc levels and function.
HDLc biology is complex and is influenced by multiple factors, including diet, environment and genetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HDL is a dynamic protein complex that responds to inflammatory cytokine signals, and is physically modified by these signals.
the pro‐inflammatory cytokines, IL‐6, TNF‐α and IL‐1β, have a profound effect on the HDLc particle.
the cytokines TNF‐α and IL‐1β have a profound effect on the biogenesis of HDLc and its subsequent clearance from the circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HDLc can be modified by pro‐inflammatory cytokine exposure and that this is likely to have a negative impact on HDLc's ability to function as a cholesterol acceptors and transporters.
HDLc may serve as an important biomarker for inflammation and that inflammation may be a contributing factor to low HDLc and cardiovascular disease.
inflammation is a key regulator of high‐density lipid (HDL) metabolism and function, and this is a major factor in the development of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.
